mainTopic: Who gets a consecrated ancestral field (שדה אחוזה) at the יובל, and whether the כהנים must pay for it: the sources behind the opinions of רבי יהודה, רבי שמעון, and רבי אליעזר
overview: This amud first finishes explaining why רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון learn from different sources. רבי יהודה compares the consecrated field to a consecrated house, since both are בדק הבית, so the כהנים pay. רבי שמעון compares it to the שבועות lambs, since both are gifts to the כהנים, so the כהנים get it free. Then the גמרא asks for the source of רבי אליעזר, who says the כהנים neither take the field nor pay. רבה splits the פסוק into two cases, but אביי rejects cutting a verse apart. אביי instead brings a ברייתא on the word 'עוד', but the גמרא shows that this ברייתא fits all opinions: it is about a field a כהן consecrated. Along the way, a second ברייתא and a list of which phrases are needed show that 'לא יגאל', 'לאשר קנהו' and 'עוד' each teach their own rule. Finally רבא gives רבי אליעזר's source: 'בצאתו' means the field goes to the כהנים only when it goes out from another person's hand.

steps.title: Why רבי יהודה does not learn from the altar offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns from a consecrated house and not from the שבועות lambs. The reason is that you compare a בדק הבית item to another בדק הבית item, not to something offered on the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: [One derives items consecrated for Temple maintenance] from items consecrated for Temple maintenance, but one does not derive items consecrated for Temple maintenance from items consecrated for the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering a question it asked just before: why doesn't רבי יהודה learn his rule from the two lambs of שבועות? The answer is that a consecrated field belongs to בדק הבית, so it should be compared to another בדק הבית item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A consecrated field is holy for Temple upkeep, not for the altar. So רבי יהודה learns from a consecrated house, which is also בדק הבית, and the כהנים pay for the field just as a house is paid for. The שבועות lambs are קדשי מזבח, a different kind of holiness, so they are not a good match.

keyTerms.meaning: The Temple maintenance fund; items given for the upkeep of the Temple
Items consecrated to be offered on the altar
We derive or compare, meaning we learn one law from another
A teaching learned from the same word appearing in two places in the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: This line begins in the middle of a sentence. Its start, 'one derives items consecrated for Temple maintenance,' comes right before it on the daf.

phrases.english: [One derives items consecrated for Temple maintenance] from items consecrated for Temple maintenance,
but one does not derive items consecrated for Temple maintenance
from items consecrated for the altar.
phrases.notes: These are the two lambs of שבועות, which רבי שמעון uses as his source.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין דָּנִין קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת מִקׇּדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer to the question asked before this text: why doesn't רבי יהודה learn from the שבועות lambs?
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picking the closer comparison, based on the type of holiness
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה could have learned from the שבועות lambs, which go to the כהנים without payment.
steps.terutzMaskana: A בדק הבית item is learned only from another בדק הבית item, so the source is the consecrated house.

steps.title: Challenge: why doesn't רבי שמעון learn from a consecrated house?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now turns the question around. Why doesn't רבי שמעון also learn from a consecrated house, the way רבי יהודה does?
steps.simpleTranslation: And let רבי שמעון also derive it from one who consecrates a house!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון with the same kind of question it asked about רבי יהודה. If the consecrated house is a good source, why doesn't רבי שמעון use it too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We were just told that a בדק הבית item should be compared to another בדק הבית item. That reasoning seems to favor the consecrated house. So רבי שמעון's choice of the שבועות lambs now looks weak, and the גמרא asks him to explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, too
Let him learn or derive
One who consecrates a house to the Temple

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon too,
let him derive it from one who consecrates a house!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן נָמֵי, נֵילַף מִמַּקְדִּישׁ בַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same logic as Step 1, now pointed at רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's choice of the שבועות lambs as his source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Step 1 showed that the consecrated house is the better match for a בדק הבית field. So why would רבי שמעון not use it?

steps.title: רבי שמעון compares one gift to the כהנים with another
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון looks at a different feature. The field goes to the כהנים as a gift, so he compares it to another gift to the כהנים, not to a house that never goes to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: One derives an item that is a gift to the priests from an item that is a gift to the priests, but one does not derive an item that is a gift to the priests from an item that is not a gift to the priests.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי שמעון. For him, the most important feature of the field is that it ends up as a gift to the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each תנא picks the feature he thinks matters most. רבי יהודה looks at the type of holiness (בדק הבית). רבי שמעון looks at where the item ends up (with the כהנים). The שבועות lambs go to the כהנים for free, so the כהנים get the field without paying.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift given to the priests
An item or thing

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה compares בדק הבית to בדק הבית, so the כהנים pay, like for a house. רבי שמעון compares a gift to the כהנים with another gift to the כהנים, so the כהנים get it free, like the שבועות lambs.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains exactly why the two תנאים disagree in the משנה about whether the כהנים must pay. Each one chooses a different feature as the basis for his comparison.

phrases.english: One derives an item that is a gift to the priests
phrases.notes: This is the ancestral field, which goes to the כהנים at the יובל.

phrases.english: from an item that is a gift to the priests,
but one does not derive an item that is a gift to the priests
from an item that is not a gift to the priests.
phrases.notes: This is the consecrated house, which never goes to the כהנים.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּנִין דָּבָר שֶׁמַּתָּנָה לַכֹּהֲנִים מִדָּבָר שֶׁמַּתָּנָה לַכֹּהֲנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Choosing a different feature as the basis for the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The consecrated house seems to be the obvious source for any בדק הבית item.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי שמעון, the feature that matters is 'gift to the כהנים,' so the שבועות lambs are the better match.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the כהנים neither take the field nor pay
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the third opinion in the משנה. רבי אליעזר says the כהנים do not take possession of the field and do not pay its value.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: They do not enter, and they do not give.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up the next line of the משנה so it can explain it. This is a setup for the question that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said the כהנים take the field and pay. רבי שמעון said they take it without paying. רבי אליעזר goes further and says the כהנים do not get the field at all at this יובל, so the question of paying never comes up.

keyTerms.meaning: They enter, meaning the כהנים take possession of the field
They give, meaning they pay the field's value to the Temple treasury
An ancestral field, land inherited from one's family

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
They do not enter, and they do not give.
phrases.notes: 'They' means the כהנים. They don't take the field, and they don't pay for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: לֹא נִכְנָסִין, וְלֹא נוֹתְנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון to the third opinion in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If no one redeemed the consecrated ancestral field before the יובל, the כהנים do not take it and do not pay for it.

steps.title: רבה asks for רבי אליעזר's reason
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks what source or reasoning stands behind רבי אליעזר's opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: What is the reason of רבי אליעזר?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה asks where רבי אליעזר's rule comes from. This sets up the answer from the פסוק in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain reading of the פסוק seems to say the field goes to the כהנים at the יובל. That makes רבי אליעזר's view surprising, so it needs a source.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: Rabba said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling quoted in Step 4
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for רבי אליעזר's view that the כהנים do not receive the field

steps.title: The פסוק read as two separate statements
steps.stepSummary: רבה quotes the פסוק and regroups its parts. The phrase 'it shall not be redeemed anymore' goes with the case where the field was not redeemed. The phrase 'when it goes out in the יובל' goes only with the case where the field was sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse states: 'And if he will not redeem the field, it shall not be redeemed anymore; and if he sold the field, the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee [shall be holy... for the priest].'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers by quoting the פסוק in a regrouped order. This shows that the field goes to the כהנים only if it was sold to someone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר splits the פסוק into two separate cases. If the owner simply did not redeem it, it 'shall not be redeemed anymore,' and nothing more is said. Only in the case of 'if he sold the field' does the פסוק continue that it goes out at the יובל to the כהנים, so an unsold field does not go to the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: He will redeem, meaning buy the field back from הקדש
The Jubilee year, every fiftieth year, when fields return

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: an ancestral field goes to the כהנים at the יובל only if it was first sold to someone else. If it was simply not redeemed, the כהנים do not get it.
steps.confusionAlert: In the Torah the phrase 'it shall not be redeemed anymore' comes after 'if he sold the field to another man.' רבה deliberately moves it next to 'if he will not redeem,' so don't expect the order to match the חומש.

phrases.english: The verse states:
'And if he will not redeem the field
it shall not be redeemed anymore,
phrases.notes: In the חומש these words come later. רבה pulls them up to go with 'if he will not redeem.'

phrases.english: and if he sold the field
the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee.'
phrases.notes: The פסוק continues that it then belongs to the כהן. Only the 'sold' case reaches that ending.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: וְאִם לֹא יִגְאַל אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה לֹא יִגָּאֵל עוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's question in Step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק is split into two cases. The rule of going out to the כהנים at the יובל applies only when the field was sold to another person.

steps.title: אביי rejects cutting the verse into pieces
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects to רבה's approach. You can't chop a פסוק apart as if with a knife and reattach its phrases to different cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Does a sharp knife cut the verses apart?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects רבה's answer from Step 6, which split the פסוק and regrouped its parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה attached 'it shall not be redeemed anymore' to one case and 'when it goes out in the יובל' to another case. אביי says a פסוק reads as one connected unit and can't be sliced up like that. So רבי אליעזר's source is still missing.

keyTerms.meaning: A sharp knife
Cuts the verses apart

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Does a sharp knife cut the verses apart?
phrases.notes: He's poking at רבה's idea from the last step of splitting the פסוק into separate pieces.

steps.triggerLanguage: סַכִּינָא חֲרִיפָא מַפְסְקָא קְרָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's reading of the פסוק given in Step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבה's entire derivation for רבי אליעזר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It splits a single פסוק and reattaches its phrases to different cases, which is not a valid way to read a verse.

steps.title: אביי's new source: a ברייתא on the word 'anymore'
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a ברייתא. 'Not redeemed anymore' means the field can't return to how it was, but it can be redeemed as a שדה מקנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: רבי אליעזר's reason is like a ברייתא. 'It shall not be redeemed.' You might think it can't be redeemed at all, even to be his like a purchased field. So the פסוק says 'anymore': it can't be redeemed to be as it was, but it can be redeemed to be his like a purchased field.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a new answer to רבה's question about רבי אליעזר's source by quoting a ברייתא that reads the word 'עוד'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'עוד' limits the ban on redemption. The owner can't get the field back as a full שדה אחוזה, but he can redeem it as a שדה מקנה. The next steps will show why this supports רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: A purchased field, which goes back to its original family at יובל
'One might have thought', which opens a possible mistaken reading
'The verse teaches', which brings the word that corrects that reading
'Anymore', the extra word being explained
To be as it was before

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
The reason of Rabbi Eliezer is as it is taught in a baraita:
"It shall not be redeemed"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:20

phrases.english: One might think it cannot be redeemed at all,
even to be his like a purchased field?
So the verse says "anymore":
to be as it was, it cannot be redeemed,
phrases.notes: 'As it was' means as his family's own ancestral field.

phrases.english: but it can be redeemed
to be his like a purchased field.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר כִּדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבה's rejected source with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר's source is the ברייתא's reading of 'עוד': the field can't return as ancestral land but can be redeemed as a purchased field.

steps.title: The ברייתא must be about the second יובל
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks when the ברייתא's case happens. It can't be the first יובל, because then the field would still be redeemable as a full שדה אחוזה. So it must be the second יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: When? If we say in the first יובל, why can't it be redeemed as it was? It's still an ancestral field! Rather, it's obviously in the second יובל.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pins down the time frame of the ברייתא. This sets up his proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the first יובל, an owner who redeems his field gets it back as full ancestral land. So the ruling 'not as it was' can't apply then. It must be talking about a later time, the second יובל.

keyTerms.meaning: When?
The first יובל cycle after the field was consecrated
An ancestral field inherited in the family
It is obvious

phrases.english: When?
If we say in the first Jubilee cycle,
why can it not be redeemed as it was?
It is still an ancestral field!
Rather, it is obviously in the second Jubilee cycle.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַת? אִילֵּימָא בְּיוֹבֵל רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא from Step 8 to fix its time frame.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In which יובל cycle is the ברייתא's case taking place?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In the second יובל, since in the first the field is still fully redeemable as ancestral land.

steps.title: Only רבי אליעזר fits, so this is his source
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון hold the field already went to the כהנים at the first יובל. Only רבי אליעזר has it still redeemable in the second יובל, so the ברייתא is his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to whom? If we say רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, the field already went to the כהנים! Rather, isn't it רבי אליעזר? Learn from this that רבי אליעזר's reason comes from here.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his proof that the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר and is the source for his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, the field leaves הקדש at the first יובל. So there is nothing left to redeem in the second יובל. Only רבי אליעזר keeps the field in הקדש that long, so the ברייתא must be his.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom?
It goes out (to the כהנים)
Learn from this, a conclusion drawn from the proof

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's argument: the ברייתא is about the second יובל, which only makes sense for רבי אליעזר. So 'עוד' would be רבי אליעזר's source.

phrases.english: And according to whom?
If we say according to Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon,
the field already goes out to the priests!
phrases.notes: For them, that happens at the first יובל, so it can't still be redeemed later.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it Rabbi Eliezer?
And learn from this
that Rabbi Eliezer's reason comes from here.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן? אִילֵימָא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the second-יובל reading to tie the ברייתא to רבי אליעזר.
steps.raayaObject: That 'עוד' is the source for רבי אליעזר's view
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on 'עוד', read as dealing with the second יובל

steps.title: What would רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון learn from 'anymore'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי. If 'עוד' belongs only to רבי אליעזר, what do רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון do with that word?
steps.simpleTranslation: And can you really think that? What do רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון learn from this word 'anymore'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's proof by asking what the other תנאים do with the word 'עוד'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the פסוק needs to teach something for all opinions. If the ברייתא belonged only to רבי אליעזר, 'עוד' would teach nothing for רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון. So the ברייתא probably fits their view too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And can you think so?', which opens a challenge
They learn out (from a word in the פסוק)

phrases.english: And can you really think that?
Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon:
what do they learn from this word "anymore"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִסְבְּרָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הַאי ״עוֹד״ מַאי דָּרְשִׁי בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the ברייתא follows only רבי אליעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If so, the word 'עוד' would teach nothing for רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון. So the ברייתא must have a reading that fits them too.

steps.title: The ברייתא fits all views: a כהן consecrated the field
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is about a field that already went to the כהנים. A כהן then made it הקדש, and the original owners came to redeem it. This works for רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what case are we dealing with here? A field that went out to the כהנים, and a כהן consecrated it, and the original owners came to redeem it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the ברייתא as a different case, so it no longer proves anything for רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even for רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, the field went to a כהן and then became הקדש again when the כהן consecrated it. If the original owners redeem it now, 'עוד' teaches they get it only as a שדה מקנה, not as their ancestral land. So the ברייתא is not רבי אליעזר's source.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What case are we dealing with here?', which narrows a text to a specific case
He consecrated it
The original owners
To redeem it

steps.confusionAlert: The ruling of the ברייתא doesn't change. It is still 'not as it was, but as a purchased field'. Only the case it describes changes, and that is what removes the proof for רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי's proof falls away. 'עוד' teaches a rule all opinions agree on, about a field a כהן consecrated, so it can't be רבי אליעזר's source. רבא gives his actual source in Step 22.

phrases.english: Rather, what case are we dealing with here?
With a field that went out to the priests,
and a priest consecrated it,
and the owners came to redeem it.
phrases.notes: The 'owners' here are the original family who first consecrated the field, not the כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 11 by giving the ברייתא a case that fits רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, which undoes אביי's proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's proof from the ברייתא for רבי אליעזר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא doesn't have to be about the second יובל under רבי אליעזר. It can describe a field a כהן consecrated, which fits every opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about the second יובל and follows only רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a field given to a כהן and then consecrated by him, and it fits all opinions.

steps.title: Why 'עוד' is needed: the owners may still redeem it as a purchased field
steps.stepSummary: Without 'עוד' we would think the original owners cannot redeem the field at all. 'עוד' teaches that it does not go back to them as it was, but they can redeem it as a שדה מקנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: it can't be redeemed at all, not even as a purchased field. So the פסוק says 'עוד' ('anymore'). It can't be redeemed to become what it was before, but it can be redeemed as a purchased field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer from step 12. It explains what the word 'עוד' teaches according to רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12 the case was a field that already went to the כהנים, and then a כהן made it הקדש. 'לא יגאל' alone might mean the original owners have no way at all to redeem it. 'עוד' limits this: it never becomes their שדה אחוזה again, but they may redeem it as a שדה מקנה, which they keep only until the next יובל.

steps.whatToRemember: For everyone, 'עוד' means the field never goes back to being the owners' family field, but they can still redeem it as a purchased field.

steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'לאשר קנהו מאתו'. We might think the field goes back to the גזבר it was bought from, so the פסוק adds 'to the one who owns the land as his family field'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught: 'In the יובל year the field returns to the one he bought it from.' You might think it returns to the הקדש treasurer he bought it from. So the פסוק says: 'to the one whose family land it is.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the case from step 12. This first part sets up the ברייתא by explaining one פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone made a purchased field הקדש and then redeemed it from the גזבר. 'The one he bought it from' could sound like the גזבר. The ending of the פסוק shows it goes back to the family owner who first sold the field.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק need the words 'to the one he bought it from'?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: if the field goes to the family owner, the פסוק could have said only 'לאשר לו אחזת הארץ'. Why does it also say 'לאשר קנהו מאתו'?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the פסוק just say 'to the one whose family land it is.' Why does it also say 'to the one he bought it from'?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, a question is asked about extra words in the פסוק. This sets up the case the ברייתא will teach next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the end of the פסוק already sends the field to the family owner, the words 'לאשר קנהו מאתו' look extra. The ברייתא assumes extra words must teach a separate case.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it say (the פסוק could have said only this)

To the one from whom he bought it

steps.title: A כהן's field that was sold, made הקדש, and redeemed goes back to the כהן
steps.stepSummary: The extra words teach a case. A field went to the כהנים, a כהן sold it, the buyer made it הקדש, and someone else redeemed it. At יובל it goes back to the כהן who sold it, not to the original owners.
steps.simpleTranslation: Take a field that went to the כהנים. A כהן sold it, the buyer made it הקדש, and someone else redeemed it. You might think it goes back to the original owners. So the פסוק says: 'to the one he bought it from', meaning the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question. 'לאשר קנהו' is for a field that the כהנים already received.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the field went to the כהנים, it belongs to them as their own family field. So at יובל it goes back to the כהן who sold it, and the first owners lose it for good. This matches step 12's case, a field that went to the כהנים and was then made הקדש, so it supports that reading for רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Went out to the כהנים (at יובל, because no one redeemed it)

The buyer

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'the one he bought it from' is the כהן, not the original family and not the גזבר.
steps.whatToRemember: Once a field has gone to the כהנים, it is the כהן's family field. At יובל it goes back to him, not to the first owners.

steps.title: Both 'לא יגאל' and 'לאשר קנהו' are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the תורה needed to write both 'לא יגאל' and 'לאשר קנהו', even though they seem to teach the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words 'it shall not be redeemed' were needed, and the words 'to the one he bought it from' were also needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says both פסוקים are needed. This sets up an explanation of why each one is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both phrases seem to teach the same thing: once a field goes to the כהנים, the first owners never get it back as their family field. The גמרא says each one still teaches something of its own, and it will explain this next.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed
It shall not be redeemed (ויקרא 27:20)
To write

phrases.english: And "it shall not be redeemed" was needed,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:20

phrases.english: and it was also needed to write "to the one from whom he bought it."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״, וְאִיצְטְרִיכָא לְמִיכְתַּב ״לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא, the גמרא notes that both פסוקים seem to say the same thing, yet both are needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both 'לא יגאל' and 'לאשר קנהו' are needed.

steps.title: Why 'לאשר קנהו' is needed even though we have 'לא יגאל'
steps.stepSummary: From 'לא יגאל' alone, we might think the rule only applies where the field never returns to anyone. Where the field does return at יובל, it might go back to the very first owner. So 'לאשר קנהו' is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the תורה had written only 'It shall not be redeemed,' I would say that is only where the field does not return at all. But here, where it does return, maybe it should go back to its first owner. So the תורה wrote 'to the one from whom it was bought.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first half of why both phrases are needed. It shows what we would get wrong if we only had 'לא יגאל'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לא יגאל' deals with a case where the field does not go back to its owner at all. The case of 'לאשר קנהו' is different: the field does return at יובל, and the only question is to whom. Without 'לאשר קנהו' we would send it to the first family owner, so the פסוק tells us it goes to the כהן who sold it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

To the one from whom it was bought

steps.title: Why 'לא יגאל' is needed even though we have 'לאשר קנהו'
steps.stepSummary: From 'לאשר קנהו' alone, we might think the first owners lose the field only because they paid nothing. Where they paid to redeem it from הקדש, maybe it stays with them. So 'לא יגאל' is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה had written only 'to the one from whom it was bought,' I would say that is because the owners did not pay any money. But here, where they do pay money, maybe it should stay with them. So the תורה wrote 'It shall not be redeemed.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of the explanation. The גמרא shows what we would get wrong if we only had 'לאשר קנהו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the 'לאשר קנהו' case, the first owners paid nothing for the field, so it makes sense that they don't get it back. In the 'לא יגאל' case, the first owners paid הקדש to redeem it, so we might think they earned it back as their family field. 'לא יגאל' teaches that even paying does not bring it back to them as it was.

keyTerms.meaning: The owners, here meaning the original family owners
They give money (pay for it)

but here, where they do pay money,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the two-way explanation that Step 18 began.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לא יגאל' is needed for the case where the first owner paid to redeem the field. Even then, it does not return to him as his family field.
steps.whatToRemember: Each phrase covers a case the other could not cover. 'לאשר קנהו' covers a field that returns at יובל where the owner did not pay. 'לא יגאל' covers a field the owner did pay for.

steps.title: Why the word 'עוד' is needed
steps.stepSummary: Without 'עוד', we would think the first owner can never redeem the field at all. 'עוד' teaches that he cannot get it back as his family field, but he can redeem it as a purchased field.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה had written 'It shall not be redeemed' without 'anymore,' I would have said it can't be redeemed at all. So the תורה wrote 'anymore': it is not redeemed to be as it was, but it is redeemed to be like a purchased field for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the reason for the word 'עוד' (as in Step 13). This finishes showing that 'לא יגאל', 'לאשר קנהו', and 'עוד' each teach their own rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לא יגאל' alone sounds like a complete ban on redeeming. Adding 'עוד' limits the ban: he cannot get it back as a שדה אחוזה, but he may redeem it as a שדה מקנה. Since 'עוד' is used up for this, it cannot be the source for the earlier view.

keyTerms.meaning: Anymore, again

A purchased field, which returns to its seller at יובל
To be as it was before (a family field)

steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'עוד' teaches that the first owner may redeem the field only as a שדה מקנה, not as his family field.

steps.title: So what is the final source?
steps.stepSummary: Both earlier sources for רבי אליעזר have fallen away. אביי rejected רבה's split reading, and 'עוד' turned out to teach a rule everyone agrees with. The גמרא asks what the conclusion is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the conclusion about it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what we end up with, since the earlier proofs have been pushed aside. This sets up רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's reading was rejected because it cuts the פסוק apart. 'עוד' has its own teaching that fits all views, so it can't be the source for רבי אליעזר either. The question asks for a new source for רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the conclusion about it?

phrases.english: What is the conclusion about it?
phrases.notes: רבה's reading and אביי's reading have both been pushed aside, so we still need a source for רבי אליעזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הָוֵי עֲלַהּ

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי אליעזר's view, now that רבה's split reading was rejected and 'עוד' is used for another teaching.

steps.title: רבא: 'בצאתו' means going out from another person's hand
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings the word 'בצאתו', 'when it goes out', in the יובל פסוק. It teaches that the field goes to the כהנים only when it leaves the hand of someone else who redeemed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the פסוק says 'And the field, when it goes out in the יובל.' 'When it goes out' means going out from the hand of another person.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the final source. The field goes to the כהנים only when it leaves someone else's possession at יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Going out' assumes the field was in someone's hands. רבא reads this as the hand of another person who redeemed it. If the field was never redeemed, it is not 'going out' from anyone, so it does not go to the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: When it goes out
From the hand (possession) of another person
The fiftieth year, when fields go back

steps.whatToRemember: The final source for רבי אליעזר is 'בצאתו', not רבה's split reading and not 'עוד'. The field goes to the כהנים only when it leaves the hand of someone else who redeemed it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It settles רבי אליעזר's source after רבה's reading was rejected and 'עוד' was given another job. It shows how the גמרא gives each word of the פסוק its own job.
